name: Learn: Custom Resources (CRDs)
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration and Security (25%). Goal: discover and use resources that extend Kubernetes — define a CustomResourceDefinition, create and inspect its custom resources, discover a CRD already installed on the cluster, and understand CRD-vs-CR lifecycle.
description: Kubernetes is extensible: a CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) teaches the API server a brand-new kind, and you then create custom resources (CRs) of that kind just like built-in objects. Learn to author a CRD, create and inspect CRs, discover CRDs already on a cluster, and reason about their lifecycle.

questions.title: Define a CustomResourceDefinition
questions.teach:
A **CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)** registers a brand-new *kind* with the API server. In `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` you set `spec.group`, `spec.names` (`kind`/`plural`/`singular`), `spec.scope`, a `versions[]` entry (`served`/`storage`), and a `schema.openAPIV3Schema`. The schema types `spec.size` (integer) and `spec.color` (string).

**Gotcha:** `metadata.name` **MUST** be exactly `<plural>.<group>` (here `widgets.stable.example.com`) — any other name is rejected.
questions.prompt:
Create a CRD so the cluster understands a new namespaced kind `Widget` in group `stable.example.com` (plural `widgets`), version `v1`, served and storage, with a schema that allows `spec.size` (integer) and `spec.color` (string).

Target: `kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com` shows the CRD with its `Established` condition `True`.
questions.hint: Apply a `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` CustomResourceDefinition. `metadata.name` must be `<plural>.<group>` = `widgets.stable.example.com`. Under `spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema` give `type: object` with `properties.spec` an object having `size` (type integer) and `color` (type string).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    kind: Widget
    plural: widgets
    singular: widget
    shortNames: [wg]
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              size:
                type: integer
              color:
                type: string
YAML
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'   # True

verification.description: CRD widgets.stable.example.com exists and is Established

questions.title: Create a custom resource
questions.teach:
Once a CRD is Established, you create its custom resources (CRs) like any native object: `kubectl apply -f`. The CR's `kind` is the CRD's `names.kind` (`Widget`) and its `spec` must match the published schema. Because this CRD is `Namespaced`, the CR lives in a namespace (`-n crd-learn`).

**Gotcha:** the CR's `apiVersion` is `<group>/<version>` (`stable.example.com/v1`), **not** `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` — that belongs to the CRD itself.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `crd-learn`, create a custom resource of kind `Widget` named `gadget` with `spec.size: 3` and `spec.color: blue`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget` exists with `.spec.size == 3` and `.spec.color == blue`.
questions.hint: `apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1`, `kind: Widget`, `metadata.name: gadget`, then a `spec` block with `size: 3` and `color: blue`. Apply it into `-n crd-learn`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: gadget
spec:
  size: 3
  color: blue
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}/{.spec.color}'   # 3/blue

verification.description: Widget 'gadget' exists in crd-learn with size=3 color=blue

questions.title: Discover a CRD already on the cluster
questions.teach:
On a real cluster, operators install their own CRDs that you must discover with no prior knowledge. Find them with `kubectl get crd | grep gizmo` or `kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com`, then read the schema via `kubectl get crd gizmos.demo.example.com -o yaml`. Create CRs against the discovered `group/version`.

**Gotcha:** the CR's `apiVersion` is the CRD's group plus the version where `served: true` (`demo.example.com/v1`) — read it off the CRD, don't guess.
questions.prompt:
The setup already installed a CRD for kind `Gizmo` in group `demo.example.com` (plural `gizmos`, namespaced, `spec.power` is an integer). Discover it, then create a `Gizmo` named `turbo` in `crd-learn` with `spec.power: 9`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get gizmo turbo` exists with `.spec.power == 9`.
questions.hint: Find it: `kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com` or `kubectl get crd | grep gizmo`. Inspect the schema: `kubectl get crd gizmos.demo.example.com -o yaml`. Then apply a `demo.example.com/v1` `Gizmo` with `spec.power: 9`.
questions.solution:
kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com
kubectl get crd gizmos.demo.example.com -o yaml | grep -A6 openAPIV3Schema
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: demo.example.com/v1
kind: Gizmo
metadata:
  name: turbo
spec:
  power: 9
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get gizmo turbo -o jsonpath='{.spec.power}'   # 9

verification.description: Gizmo 'turbo' (seeded CRD) exists in crd-learn with power=9

questions.title: List custom resources by plural / short name
questions.teach:
Because a CRD registers a real kind, you list its CRs with the same verbs as native objects: `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` (plural), `get widget` (singular), or `get wg` (short name) all return the same objects. Add another Widget and both show up.

**Gotcha:** for a Namespaced CRD, forgetting `-n` lists only the current/`default` namespace, so the resources can look "empty" when they really exist elsewhere.
questions.prompt:
Create a **second** Widget named `widget2` in `crd-learn` (`spec.size: 7`, `spec.color: red`), so that listing with `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` shows two Widgets.

Target: namespace `crd-learn` contains at least two Widgets, including `widget2`.
questions.hint: Same shape as step 2 but `metadata.name: widget2`, `size: 7`, `color: red`. Verify with `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` (or the short name `kubectl -n crd-learn get wg`).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: widget2
spec:
  size: 7
  color: red
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets   # gadget and widget2
kubectl -n crd-learn get wg        # same, via shortName

questions.title: CR vs CRD lifecycle
questions.teach:
A custom resource (CR) and the CRD that defines it have independent lifecycles. Deleting a single CR with `kubectl -n crd-learn delete widget scratch` removes only that object — the CRD and every sibling Widget stay intact.

**Gotcha:** deleting the CRD itself (`kubectl delete crd widgets.stable.example.com`) is the heavy hammer — it garbage-collects every CR of that kind cluster-wide, across all namespaces. Delete one CR to clean up data; delete the CRD only to retire the whole kind.
questions.prompt:
A CR's lifecycle is independent of its CRD and of its sibling CRs. Create a throwaway Widget `scratch` in `crd-learn` (any size/color), then delete **only** `scratch`.

Target: `scratch` is gone, while the CRD `widgets.stable.example.com`, `gadget`, and `widget2` all remain.
questions.hint: Apply a Widget named `scratch`, then `kubectl -n crd-learn delete widget scratch`. Deleting one CR leaves the CRD and the other CRs (`gadget`, `widget2`) untouched — only deleting the CRD itself cascade-deletes every Widget.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: scratch
spec:
  size: 1
  color: green
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn delete widget scratch
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets                 # gadget and widget2 remain
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com       # CRD still present

verification.description: scratch deleted; CRD, gadget, and widget2 all survive
